items.heading: Ask Which Specific Track Your
items.text: Ask which specific track your child means, not just the subject name. A parent hearing "home science" and picturing only cooking classes is working from an outdated picture. Ask whether the direction is dietetics, food technology, design, child development, extension work, or something else.

items.heading: Compare the Real Pay
items.text: Compare the real pay and timeline honestly, track by track. Food technology pays sooner than dietetics private practice. A government role is stable but capped. Do not let one prestige assumption about "home science" decide the whole conversation.

items.heading: Ask What Proof of Work
items.text: Ask what proof of work exists before spending heavily on college. A portfolio piece, a real internship, or one completed proof task tells you more about fit than a college brochure does.

items.heading: Do Not Dismiss IT As
items.text: Do not dismiss it as a fallback subject. Home science leads to regulated, government-recognised, and genuinely well-paid corporate careers when the right track is chosen and skill-building continues past the degree.
